correctness.rationale: The permanent-white-cycle invariant and no-first-move spanning-tree obstruction exclude all other white-edge graphs. For every disconnected forest, an external blue edge from a white leaf has a unique white neighbor in its white component; repeatedly removing leaf edges forces every white vertex. Labeled set partitions and Cayley trees count the entire class. The embedded direct PSD simulator exhausts every initial coloring for n=3..6 (33864) and an independent partition/acyclicity checker verifies exact coefficients through n=8.

originality.rationale: The known Z_+(J(n,2)) scalar in Peters 2012 Proposition 3.16 and Fallat et al. 2015 Lemma 8.3 is explicitly prior. The complete forest iff criterion for every PSD initial set, full polynomial and counts for all minimum sets are more informative and are not implied by these scalar statements. Known ordinary forcing of the same graph is stronger and has fewer successful sets. Actual semantic searches and highly relevant original texts were examined; historical-priority risk from unindexed text remains.

value.rationale: A natural exact enumerator for every PSD zero forcing set of an infinite graph family is a distinct invariant from the known minimum size. The iff disconnected-forest characterization is structural, gives a uniform counting method and a natural two-tree optimal family, and detects a strict PSD-versus-ordinary gap with exact counts starting at four labels. Its self-contained all-parameter proof and reproducible small enumerations make the result useful independent of whether it yields a downstream theorem.
